title: Why I Built Is the Ferry Running?
excerpt: The creator developed a forecasting tool addressing a persistent challenge for Martha's Vineyard residents: determining whether ferries will actually operate given current conditions.
content:
The creator developed a forecasting tool addressing a persistent challenge for Martha's Vineyard residents: determining whether ferries will actually operate given current conditions, not merely checking published schedules.

The fundamental problem stems from a gap between official timetables and real-world maritime conditions. Weather patterns offshore differ significantly from land-based forecasts, and port-specific geography creates varied exposure levels. Ferry cancellations often occur despite seemingly adequate conditions, leaving commuters, families, and travelers caught off-guard.

The solution combines historical performance data, marine weather analysis, port geography, and seasonal patterns to generate probability assessments. The system evaluates six primary ports—Woods Hole, Hyannis, Falmouth, Vineyard Haven, Oak Bluffs, and Nantucket—treating each location's distinct characteristics separately rather than uniformly.

Importantly, the platform complements rather than replaces official operator decisions. It functions as an informational resource helping people anticipate disruptions proactively rather than reacting after cancellations occur.

For residents managing daily commutes and medical appointments, clearer risk assessment enables better scheduling decisions. Travelers benefit from more realistic expectations about same-day island accessibility.

The project explicitly remains independent—unaffiliated with ferry operators, non-commercial, and locally developed by someone experiencing these transportation challenges firsthand.

**Live site:** https://www.istheferryrunning.com

title: Something Broken in Your iPhone, Who Ya Gonna Call? Louis Hall
excerpt: A Martha's Vineyard Gazette article about Louis Hall, founder of Anything Apple, highlighting his journey from childhood fascination with disassembling electronics to launching a successful repair business.
content:
A Martha's Vineyard Gazette article about Louis Hall, founder of Anything Apple. The piece highlights Hall's journey from childhood fascination with disassembling electronics to launching a successful repair business.

Hall started the company nine years prior at his home office while teaching environmental science. He holds Apple Certified Macintosh Technician credentials and initially focused on computer repairs before expanding to iPhone repairs.

Hall's interest in technology began at SUNY Oneonta, where a virus destroyed his PC hard drive during his sophomore year. His father then gifted him an iBook, sparking his technical expertise.

iPhone repairs typically take "15 minutes to two hours" depending on damage severity. Salt water causes more corrosion than fresh water, and power port repairs require more maintenance than screen replacements.

Hall emphasizes a key business advantage: "I'm able to get third-party computer parts," allowing him to offer competitive pricing compared to Apple's wholesale rates.

**Original article:** [Martha's Vineyard Gazette](https://vineyardgazette.com/news/2016/09/21/something-broken-your-iphone-who-ya-gonna-call-louis-hall)

title: Malicious iOS Popups
excerpt: Lately, I have had more and more clients coming to me with screens that look malicious, wondering if they have a virus. Here's what to do.
content:
PSA - my name is Louis Hall and for those of you who do not know me, I am the owner of Anything Apple MV.

Lately, I have had more and more clients coming to me with screens that look like malicious popups, wondering if they have a virus. Basically what you are seeing is a malicious webpage that will lead you to clicking a link that could potentially install a malicious app or lead you to giving away personal information.

## Key Points
- Apple has never, and most likely never will, ask you to call them about a problem
- Apple will never suggest that you need to install things from a webpage
- The only place Apple products will ever suggest an update is through the official App Store or through system settings

## How to Solve the Issue
If you swipe down on a typical web page you will see the tab icon at the bottom right hand side of your menu. Click that and close the malicious webpage/popup.

Until you click on the links within that webpage there is nothing that the webpage can do to install anything on your phone or computer. The only way, on an Apple product, for malicious files to be installed is if you begin pressing buttons giving the files permission to install itself.

**Don't give the bad guys permission. Just close the window. :)**

title: Weekly Tip: Start Taking Advantage of the Cloud!
excerpt: People keep talking about 'the cloud,' but most of us have no idea what it is or why we should use it. Well here is the low down...
content:
People keep talking about "the cloud," but most of us have no idea what it is or why we should use it. Well here is the low down...

## What is the Cloud?
The internet was originally referred to as "the cloud." But it was restricted to communication between computers in a building and was nothing compared to the technology of today. The idea of "the cloud" was not really even a word, it was wild hand gestures suggesting a lot of movement in an attempt to describe something that was here but not here. Kind of like air.

Think... the little lines around Pigpen's head (cough... random Snoopy references).

## How Does It Work Today?
Large companies, like Amazon, Microsoft, Apple, and others like Dropbox and Sugarsync run servers to which you send your information. By selling ad-space on their websites and through monthly storage plans for high-end users, they are able to offer off-site storage to consumers at cheap rates.

By creating an account with one of these companies you agree to having them host your data. It is like having a thumb drive that you won't forget to take out of the pocket of your jeans!

Most of them allow you to pick certain files for backing up and that's it - BAM! Once you have selected the important files for backing up to the cloud, they are continuously monitored for changes and backed up when changes occur.

This cloud account has not only saved me countless times, but many of my clients as well!

**Stop wasting time and energy on the ground and get into the Cloud!**

title: The End of an Era
excerpt: Early this morning, my 3-year-old son and I wandered into a place on Martha's Vineyard that will forever remind me of the wonder that electronics parts have always held for me.
content:
To the Editor:

Early this morning, my 3-year-old son and I wandered into a place on Martha's Vineyard that will forever remind me of the wonder that electronics parts have always held for me. In typical fashion, I strode through the doors and immediately looked for the little black dog (salt and pepper...) to greet me. Today was most likely the last time that I will walk through those doors.

Sometime in the near future, Vineyard Electronics will be closing its doors after many years of service to Islanders. The importance of this business to Island residents may not be noticed immediately, but it will be the next time you need a replacement universal remote for your TV, or quick and free consultation about how to put your SIM card into your cell phone.

The closing of this business is a reminder to us all, and I am guilty, about the impact that purchasing from Amazon and other e-commerce businesses has on small communities. The day of the "mom and pop" businesses is coming to an end at the hand of the convenience that these companies offer. I remember when Hollywood Video closed, and how I couldn't understand how Netflix had really done them in. This is the same thing, and I, honestly, feel quite guilty. I'm not sure how to reach a balance in both worlds, but I do know that if we are not aware of our actions, we cannot change our ways.

Thank you for keeping prices low for us, for your guidance on all things tech, and for your devotion to so many neophytes across our little Island. We will miss all of you at Vineyard Electronics.

Louis Hall,
Owner Anything iTech Martha's Vineyard
